title: OAuth application consent prompt requesting mailbox-read/write access
event_type: OAuth delegated-permission consent prompt, illustrating the disclosure language a user sees when an application requests a Mail.ReadWrite-equivalent scope (§7, OAuth consent-grant abuse)

fields.label: Publisher
fields.value: Unverified publisher — publisher domain not confirmed

fields.label: Permission disclosure text (user-facing)
fields.value: "Read, update, create, and delete email in your mailbox"

fields.label: Additional requested scope
fields.value: offline_access — "Maintain access to data you have given it access to"

callouts.explanation: An unverified-publisher badge is the single strongest visual cue at consent time that this app hasn't been reviewed by the platform vendor — the point §7 makes about the consent screen being the last real chance to stop this attack path.

The plain-language text is where most users actually make the approve/deny decision, not the technical scope name — 'read, update, create, and delete' is the same access DET-17-03's query flags via the Mail.ReadWrite/Mail.Read/Mail.Send scope list.

offline_access is what lets the resulting token keep working after the user's browser session ends, which is exactly why this attack path survives a password reset — the token itself, not a session cookie, carries the access forward.

note: This is a conceptual, illustrative mockup of consent-prompt disclosure language for teaching purposes — not a captured vendor screenshot and not attributed to any specific vendor's actual interface.
